body:
# Editorial Stylesheet — *Protocolized Anthology* (working draft)

A living reference for copy editing the stories in this series. Goal: **consistency**
across stories while preserving each author's voice. This is a *light* copy edit
regime — fix mechanics, don't rewrite. When in doubt, leave the author's choice.

Started from: *01 Aster's Story: Presence Must Preserve*

1. Author/editor exports the Google Doc as **Microsoft Word (.docx)** (keeps
   italics, smart quotes, em dashes, scene breaks). Plain-text paste loses these.
2. Drop the file in `editorial/Zoothesia/source/NN Title.docx`.

3. From `editorial/Zoothesia/`, extract for editing without losing emphasis:
   `pandoc -f docx -t markdown --wrap=none "source/NN Title.docx" -o work.md`
4. Edit `work.md` (asterisks = the author's italics; verify each one is real).
5. Render back: `pandoc -f markdown -t docx work.md -o "edited/NN Title (copyedited).docx"`

6. Deliver **clean edited .docx + a `NN-...-CHANGELOG.md`** (before → after list
   plus author queries). We do clean edits, not tracked-changes redlines
   (pandoc can't author Word revision marks reliably); the changelog is the
   review surface.

7. Sanity-check emphasis survived the round-trip:
   `pandoc -f docx -t markdown edited/....docx | grep -oP '\*[^*]+\*'`

> **Italic-export gotcha:** Google Docs sometimes extends an italic run over the
> trailing `."` of a sentence. After extraction, check that closing punctuation
> isn't accidentally inside `*...*`; move it out. (Happened once in Story 01.)
>
> **Literal asterisks:** if the author *types* `*gag*` as characters (not as an
> italic style), pandoc shows it escaped as `\*gag\*`. Preserve that — it's an
> authorial choice, not emphasis.

col2: Single glyph … or spaced periods, but be consistent within a story
Spell out zero–one hundred in prose; numerals for years, addresses, temps with units, code/UI values

body: These stories use a casual, interior first-person voice. **Keep:**
- Sentence-fragments used for rhythm/emphasis. *"Poof. There." / "Or dangerous."*
- Conversational discourse markers: "Like, sure,…", "I mean it", "I guess", "sure".
- Profanity and slang in dialogue and narration (do not soften).
- Coined/neologism vocabulary (see Lexicon). Do not “correct” invented words.
- Intentional repetition for effect (e.g., "The same… The same…").

**Fix:** grammar slips, missing/extra words, agreement errors, typos,
mistaken homophones, dropped punctuation, inconsistent styling.
When a fragment vs. error is ambiguous, preserve if it scans as deliberate.
- Each speaker gets a new paragraph.

- Put a Q&A exchange on **separate** lines/paragraphs, even when terse
  ("You've got a good job?" / "Why do you care?").

- Dialogue tags lowercase after a comma: `she said, "Let's go."` and
  `"Never," he said.`

- Capitalize the first word of quoted dialogue introduced by a comma:
  `shrugged and said, "Let's go."`

- Titles of in-world media, tracks, filters, products: *italics*.
  *Marine Serenity: Safe Waters in Your Social Seas*; *Pink Sunrises*.

- Editorial/sound asides the author types with literal asterisks (e.g. `*gag*`):
  **keep the literal asterisks** — do not convert to italics. Place sentence
  punctuation logically (in Story 01: `(... \*gag\*.)` — period inside the paren).

- Emphasis vs. punctuation: ensure trailing `.`/`,`/`"` are *outside* an italic
  span unless the author clearly intended otherwise.

- Story header banner kept verbatim as delivered:
  `= = = NN Title: Subtitle = = =`

- Scene breaks: use a blank line or `* * *` consistently (TBD per layout; the
  DOCX/Typst pipeline handles `---`).

> **Presence vs. Perception (collection-wide flag):** the marketing *slogan* is
> "Presence Must Preserve" (title case, the billboard/tagline form). The in-world
> *maxim/design principle* is "Perception must preserve(, not present)" (lowercase).
> Stories 05 and 06 use *Perception* where 02/04 use *Presence*. We lowercased the
> maxim form and title-cased the slogan form, but the Presence/Perception split
> itself is an **open author query** — see §8.

> **Action for editors:** append new coinages to this table as each story is edited.
> Flag any term that appears spelled two ways for an author query.
These were the actual corrections in Aster's Story; expect similar in others:

- **Hyphenation of compound modifiers:** taped-off, skin-deep, drug-fueled,
  ivory-colored, sickly sweetness (open as noun).
- **Possessives:** someone’s, others’ — check apostrophe placement.
- **its vs. it’s:** "its faultless humanity" (possessive), not "it's."

- **angrier** not "angier"; **desiccated** not "dessicated"; **putrefying** not
  "putrifying"; **hall pass** two words.
- **Subject/verb & there was/were:** "there were so many more people."
- **Dropped/duplicated words:** delete false starts like "I was the I couldn't…".
- **Comma before terminal "sometimes"/parentheticals** — verify.
- **"step up to the corner"** (missing preposition).

- **Question marks** on questions phrased as statements in interior monologue
  ("To judge the lives of those whose urges were completely alien?").
- **Plurals vs. names:** "shouted out the names of the body parts."
- Authorial fragments and run-ons used stylistically.
- Slang, vulgarity, and dialect in dialogue.
- Invented terminology and neologisms (style them per the Lexicon).

- Voice-driven comma splices in fast interior passages — light edit only;
  query the author rather than silently rewriting if meaning is at stake.
Raise (don't silently fix) when:
- A coined term is spelled inconsistently and you can't tell which is canonical.
- A sentence's meaning is genuinely ambiguous.

- A factual/continuity detail conflicts within or across stories
  (e.g., timeline, place names, the rules of the Zoo).
### Story 01 queries
- "an eleven-o'clock shadow" — deliberate riff on "five-o'clock shadow"? Kept as written (assumed intentional).
- "rose miasmatic" — unusual inversion; kept as stylistic. Confirm.
- "Play-pretending my father." — fragment in the saint's speech; kept as voice.
### Story 02 (Ki) queries

- Friend names **Cressida** (hardware) vs. **Clarissa** (confidante) read as two
  people — confirm distinct. "Cassandra's equation" corrected to **Clarissa's**.
- "insect scream **decimal** count" → read as **decibel** count. Confirm.
- Slogan standardized to title-case "Presence Must Preserve."
### Story 03 (Angel) queries
- Protagonist named **Heath** (once). Confirm spelling.
- Percentages kept as numerals + spelled unit ("15 percent"); confirm vs. % glyph.
- "splitting ribs" — deliberate riff on "splitting hairs." Kept.
### Story 04 (Ed) queries
- **Mayaport** vs. Mayaford — see Lexicon flag. Left as written.
- "the Market" capitalization inconsistent (Leviathan personification). Left as delivered.
- Trader shorthand "2K into 70" kept as numerals (voice).
### Story 05 (Elara & Io) queries
- "awonawon" = phonetic mishearing of "one of one." Intentional; do not correct.
- **Oren** the taxi driver — same name as the recurring dealer/fixer. Confirm.
- "Perception must preserve" lowercased to match maxim styling.
- "He's understand" → "He'd understand." Confirm.
### Story 06 (Karina) queries
- **Mayaport** vs. Mayaford — see Lexicon flag.
- "intersticed" kept as author coinage (after fixing doubled-s "instersticed").
- Presence/Perception slogan split (billboard reads "Perception must preserve").
- "Karinaic," "Zoothesetic" kept as coinages.
### Collection-wide open queries

(Each bullet is a query on the collection review page. Optional indented
`terms:` / `brief:` sub-bullets feed the auto-assembled "Context for this
ruling" block: `terms:` sets the manuscript-search phrases; `brief:` supplies
hand-written framing that overrides the auto stylesheet explanation.)

- **Presence vs. Perception** in the slogan/maxim (see §5). Needs an author ruling.
  - terms: presence must preserve; perception must preserve

- **Mayaport vs. Mayaford** as a place name (Stories 04, 06).
  - terms: Mayaport; Mayaford

- **Oren** as a deliberately recurring character across stories (01, 02, 05, 06).
  - terms: Oren

*Maintainer note:* keep this file under `editorial/Zoothesia/`. Update the Lexicon and
watch-list with every story so later stories inherit decisions made earlier.
